### Observed differences

- Three activities became optional in the later window: A22 appears in every earlier trace but in only about 54 in 100 later traces (107 of 200), and A31, A32 and A37 each appear in every earlier trace but in about 47 in 100 later traces (94 of 200), never more than once per trace in either window. A20, A21, A23 and A26 still appear in every trace in both windows [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, POS001, POS002, POS004, POS005].
- The block A31/A32/A37 is bypassed on the main path: earlier, A20's outgoing transitions led to A37 (about 35%), A31 (about 34%) and A32 (about 31%); in the later window about 995 in 1000 of them lead straight to A23, and the A20→A23 distance changed from always 4 event positions to 1 position in about 995 in 1000 later cases [DIR001, LAG001].
- When the block runs in the later window, it runs later in the trace: its mean position moved from about 0.39–0.40 to about 0.58 of the trace; earlier each of A31, A32, A37 preceded A23, A21 and A26 in 100% of traces, whereas later A23 and A21 precede them, and they precede A26, in essentially all cases where they co-occur (about 47% of traces); the block's outgoing transitions now lead to A26 (about 29–36% each) instead of to A23 [POS006, POS007, POS008, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005].
- A22 and the block became mutually exclusive alternatives after A21: earlier A21 always led to A22 and A22 always co-occurred with A31/A32/A37; in the later window A21 leads to A22 in about 54% of its outgoing transitions and to the block in about 46% (split roughly evenly across A31, A32, A37), A22 co-occurs with the block in only about 1 in 200 traces, and the A21→A26 distance is 2 positions in about 54% of later traces and 4 positions in about 46%, against always 2 earlier [DIR002, REL005, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, LAG005].
- The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A23 and A24 roughly doubled, from a mean of about 1.0 h to about 1.9 h (median about 1.02 h to about 1.94 h), with the whole distribution shifted upward by roughly 0.9–1.0 h at each quartile [TWAIT001].

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

Screening flagged 47 control-flow items against roughly 0.5 expected without a change, and 1 time item against roughly 0.01 expected, so the volume of flagged items far exceeds what an unchanged process typically produces [DIR001, REL011, OCC001, TWAIT001]. The evidence supports the hypothesis that, in the later window, the three-activity block A31/A32/A37 that previously always executed between A20 and A23 is bypassed on the direct path — A20 now leads almost always straight to A23 — and instead runs in about 47% of traces after A21 and before A26, where it is mutually exclusive with A22, which itself is skipped in about 46% of later traces. This is shown directly and consistently by participation drops, successor changes at A20, A21 and the block, flipped precedence relations with A23, A21 and A26, and the A20→A23 distance collapsing from 4 positions to adjacent [DIR001, LAG001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005, REL006, REL011, REL014, REL017, OCC001, OCC002].

Limitations: the internal ordering of the three block activities and the placement of A24 are not resolved by this evidence, and six lag items about the block's new distances rest on a single after-window case each [LAG002, LAG003, LAG004, LAG006, LAG007, LAG008]. An important competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is that the roughly 53/47 split between the A22 path and the block path reflects a changed mix of case types taking different existing paths rather than a new routing rule, since no case attributes are available [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004].

Other differences: The elapsed time between consecutive completions of A23 and A24 roughly doubled (about 1.0 h to about 1.9 h on average) — a timing change in its own right for which the evidence shows no structural counterpart [TWAIT001].

Now let's understand the behavioural story.
